data.title: Matt Godbolt sold me on Rust by showing me C++
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary:
本文由Gustavo Noronha撰写，介绍了Matt Godbolt通过C++演示让他认识到Rust的优点。文章首先赞扬了Matt在Compiler Explorer上的工作，并特别提到他的演讲《Correct by Construction: APIs That Are Easy to Use and Hard to Misuse》。作者有超过20年的C/C++经验，对演讲中提到的问题深有共鸣。

Matt在演讲中展示了一个发送股票订单的函数，指出C++中容易混淆参数类型的问题，比如用`double`表示价格和用`int`表示数量，编译器不会报错。作者尝试通过类型别名、类和显式构造函数来改进，但仍无法完全避免错误。最终，通过使用模板和静态断言，作者成功让编译器在参数错误时发出警告。

文章旨在展示Rust在类型安全方面的优势，并通过具体代码示例说明如何在C++中实现类似的保护机制。最终，通过复杂的代码改进，作者实现了编译时的类型检查。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rust与C++的比较，特别是在错误处理、类型安全、语言特性及库支持方面的差异。

不同观点：
• **Rust的错误处理优于C++**：[dvratil]认为Rust通过`Result`类型和`?`操作符使得错误处理更加一致和简便，而C++中存在多种错误处理方式，缺乏一致性，即使是标准库也是如此。
• **C++也能实现类似Rust的模式**：[thrwyexecbrain]指出，现代C++可以通过良好的设计模式（如明确的类型和生命周期管理）实现与Rust类似的代码风格，区别主要在于构建系统和编译器提示的差异。
• **Rust的防御性编程未必有效**：[antirez]认为，Rust提倡的防御性编程（如强类型）未必能提高代码质量，代码质量更多依赖于严格的测试和质量控制。
• **库的支持是关键**：[kasajian]认为，C++也能通过合适的库实现Rust的特性，因此问题不在于语言本身，而在于可用的库。
• **语言特性和库特性需区分**：[jpc0]提醒不要将语言特性和库特性混为一谈，并指出C++的隐式转换是导致一些问题的原因，而Rust没有这种问题。
• **C++有工具可以改善类型转换问题**：[grumbel]提到，C++中可以使用`-Wconversion`来捕获一些类型转换问题，但并不能解决所有情况。
• **Rust缺乏关键字参数是缺点**：[GardenLetter27]和[jsat]都提到，Rust缺乏命名参数或关键字参数，导致需要更多的样板代码。
• **简化C语言的设想**：[markus_zhang]提出，是否可以创建一种去除 quirks 的C语言变种，使其更安全但不增加复杂性。
• **Rust的内存安全优势**：[tumdum_]表示，Rust最吸引人的地方在于消除了由于内存损坏导致的Heisenbugs。

补充讨论：
• **对atoi的批评**：多个评论（如[dvratil], [writebetterc]）提到，在现代C++中不应使用`atoi`，而应使用STL中的转换函数以获得更好的错误处理。
• **Rust的学习曲线和社区资源**：[morning-coffee]提到，通过学习《Rust Book》转向了Rust，而[favorited]则提到一个与Rust相关的播客，提供了更多学习资源。

争议焦点：
• **强类型和防御性编程的价值**：一些开发者（如[antirez]）认为Rust的强类型和防御性编程未必能带来实际价值，而另一些开发者（如[dvratil], [jpc0]）则认为这些特性显著提高了代码的可靠性。
• **命名参数的必要性**：部分开发者（如[GardenLetter27], [jsat]）认为Rust缺乏命名参数是一个显著缺点，而其他开发者则未提及此问题，显示出对语言特性需求的个体差异。

data.title: Show HN: Feedsmith — Fast parser & generator for RSS, Atom, OPML feed namespaces
data.author: macieklamberski
data.article_summary: Feedsmith 是一个强大且快速的 JavaScript 解析和生成工具，支持 RSS、Atom、JSON Feed 和 RDF  feeds，同时支持 Podcast、iTunes、Dublin Core 和 OPML 文件。它提供通用和特定格式的解析器，保持原始 feed 结构，并智能规范化旧版元素。其特点包括对大小写不敏感、高性能、类型安全、树形抖动、良好的跨平台兼容性及全面的测试。支持多种格式和命名空间的解析与生成，如 Atom、Dublin Core、Syndication、Content、iTunes 等。安装通过 npm 进行，使用简便，提供通用和专用解析函数，返回对象包含所有支持的命名空间数据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：RSS工具的功能与实现方式的比较

不同观点：
• [DIYgod] 对 Feedsmith 表示兴趣，提到自己曾开发过 RSSHub 和 Folo 项目，之前使用 rss-parser 遇到问题，现在对 Feedsmith 的一些功能很感兴趣，并表示会尝试使用。这表明他对不同 RSS 工具的实际应用效果有一定关注，且愿意尝试新的解决方案。

• [renegat0x0] 赞赏项目的同时，介绍了自己开发的 RSS 阅读器，强调自己选择重新实现 RSS 阅读器的原因，包括避免多次重复实现、满足特定需求（如自动检测网站 RSS 源、提供基础元素如缩略图）。他还提到使用了 Python 和 Docker 来实现其 API 形式的 RSS 阅读器，并指出传统工具如 feedparser 在并发处理 XML 时的问题。

• [piotrkulpinski] 关注性能问题，询问是否有与类似工具包的性能对比基准测试。这表明他更在意工具的性能表现，尤其是与其他工具的横向对比。

补充讨论：
• [renegat0x0] 的项目专注于 RSS 爬虫功能，简化了用户操作（如只需处理 JSON 格式数据，无需关注 HTTP 请求、状态码等），强调了其工具在特定场景下的简便性与实用性。
• [DIYgod] 提到曾遇到 XML 相关问题，而 [renegat0x0] 也指出 feedparser 在处理 XML 并发时的缺陷，表明 XML 解析在 RSS 工具开发中是一个常见的技术难点。

Feedsmith
Robust and fast JavaScript parser and generator for RSS, Atom, JSON Feed, and RDF feeds, with support for popular namespaces and OPML files. It provides both universal and format-specific parsers that maintain the original feed structure while offering helpful normalization.
Feedsmith maintains the original feed structure in a clean, object-oriented format. It intelligently normalizes legacy elements, providing you with complete access to all feed data without compromising simplicity.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：智能眼镜在乐谱阅读中的应用及其技术实现和市场潜力

不同观点：
• MarcelOlsz认为该项目在视读（sight reading）中非常有用，尤其是对于需要频繁切换乐谱的场景，如演奏时。
• mdp2021对项目中使用的硬件和软件选择提出质疑，认为选择"Even Realities G1" AR眼镜和复杂的软件架构不如使用规格更优且价格可能更低的"Epson Moverio" AR眼镜，以及更直接的Android系统集成。
• pedalpete分享了个人使用场景，提到在演奏时需要频繁 scroll 乐谱的问题，并建议通过麦克风实现自动滚动功能，同时提出加入节拍器的想法。
• eitally提出与大型数字乐谱供应商（如Musescore或Music Notes）合作或出售项目的可能性，并设想集成更多功能如节拍调整和乐曲调性转换，认为这对钢琴演奏者有很大吸引力。
• analog31强调了适应纸质乐谱的重要性，并指出在某些音乐类型（如大乐队爵士）中，乐谱通常只有PDF格式，项目需要适应这类需求。
• floren对乐谱显示速度提出疑问，担心显示速度不足以跟上快速演奏的节奏，认为在视频中显示的乐谱条数可能不够用。
• KyleBrandt从视觉效果角度出发，希望看到在舞台上无谱演奏的场景，并提出如果智能眼镜能看起来像普通眼镜会更好。
• theyknowitsxmas以幽默的方式建议给指挥一个按钮代替30个踏板。
• paul7986对智能眼镜的实用性表示认可，特别是Meta Ray Bans，但也对其作为下一代计算平台的说法表示怀疑，认为智能眼镜更多是现有设备的补充。

补充讨论：
• 智能眼镜在乐谱阅读中的实际应用场景和用户需求（如自动滚动和节拍器功能）得到较多关注。
• 技术实现的细节，如硬件选择和软件架构的合理性，引发了对项目可行性和效率的讨论。
• 市场潜力方面，有人提出与大型乐谱供应商合作的可能性，并设想了更多功能集成以增加市场吸引力。
• 对智能眼镜的视觉效果和使用体验也有一定讨论，特别是在舞台演奏场景中的应用。
• 对智能眼镜作为通用计算平台的质疑，反映了用户对其长期市场定位和功能扩展的思考。

We’ve seen developers doing amazing things with

, so we decided to release an updated version a couple of weeks early to get into developers hands sooner.
Today we’re excited to release Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview (I/O edition). This update features even stronger coding capabilities, for you to start building with before Google I/O later this month. Expect meaningful improvements for front-end and UI development, alongside improvements in fundamental coding tasks such as transforming and editing code, and creating sophisticated agentic workflows.
“We found Gemini 2.5 Pro to be the best frontier model when it comes to "capability over latency" ratio. I look forward to rolling it out on Replit Agent whenever a latency-sensitive task needs to be accomplished with a high degree of reliability.”
–
Michele Catasta, President,
Replit
Best-in-class frontend web development
Gemini 2.5 Pro now ranks #1 on the
WebDev Arena leaderboard
, which measures human preference for a model’s ability to build aesthetically pleasing and functional web apps. Drawing on this leading capability, Gemini 2.5 Pro powers Cursor’s innovative code agent and empowers our collaborations with companies like Cognition and Replit. Together, we're pushing the frontiers of agentic programming to unlock new possibilities for developers.
“The updated Gemini 2.5 Pro achieves leading performance on our junior-dev evals. It was the first-ever model that solved one of our evals involving a larger refactor of a request routing backend. It felt like a more senior developer because it was able to make correct judgement calls and choose good abstractions.”
–
Silas Alberti, Founding Team,
Cognition
Gemini 2.5 Pro in action
Gemini 2.5 Pro’s deep understanding of code, combined with powerful reasoning, continues to make Gemini 2.5 Pro the go-to model for developers. We’re particularly excited about how this model can be used in the following cases.
Video to code
Gemini 2.5 Pro delivers state-of-the-art video understanding, scoring 84.8% on the VideoMME benchmark. Combining this with coding enables new flows that were previously not possible with previous versions. For example, the
Video to Learning App
in Google AI Studio demonstrates how Gemini 2.5 Pro creates an interactive learning app based on a single YouTube video. With improved video understanding and complete UI, the updated Gemini 2.5 Pro model delivers a more functional experience than the previous simple example.

data.article_summary: Plexe是一款通过自然语言描述来构建机器学习模型的工具。用户只需用 plain English 描述所需模型，Plexe 就能通过多智能体架构自动构建并训练模型。它支持多种LLM（大型语言模型）提供商，如OpenAI、Anthropic等，并可通过Ray进行分布式训练以加速模型生成。Plexe还具备自动数据生成和 schema 推断功能，简化了数据准备过程。安装通过 `pip install plexe` 完成，并支持多种安装选项以适应不同需求。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Plexe模型的生成过程、交互性、扩展性以及其相对于传统ML和LLM的优势和局限。

不同观点：
• Stiopa认为Plexe模型生成过程中的多个步骤应增加用户交互，让用户在每一步确认或修改计划，特别是对于复杂模型或有更高需求的用户，应该有更灵活的扩展性。

• Oras关注Plexe在处理数据清理和检测训练数据问题上的能力，并询问模型是否能够自主决定创建或微调模型。
• dweinus持怀疑态度，认为Plexe并不能解决ML的核心困难，如数据质量评估和特征设计，并提到2018年autoML的失败案例。
• fzysingularity希望看到Plexe方法相对于传统模型训练的优越性，并提到零样本性能的优势，但认为需要证明LLM在模型构建阶段的有效性。
• vessenes对agents组合的方法表示赞赏，并询问对smolagent的评价。
• drlobster询问是否可以将Plexe整合到scikit-learn兼容的pipeline中。
• srameshc诚实询问是否可以从数据集中获得微调模型。
• yu3zhou4分享了自己一年前构建的类似简单版本，并表达对Plexe推动autoML的期望。
• ratatoskrt基于经验指出人类和LLM在统计上的不足，认为LLM会模仿人类的典型错误。
• revskill提出希望看到更多基于“意图”的方法，而不仅仅是注意力机制。

补充讨论：
• 用户交互的增加：Stiopa和thefourthchime强调了用户在模型生成过程中参与和确认的重要性。
• 传统ML与LLM的平衡：gitroom和MarcoDewey对回归基础ML的赞赏，与其他评论中对LLM和自动化方法的讨论形成对比。
• 对复杂模型的支持：Oras和dweinus对Plexe在复杂模型和数据处理上的能力表示关注，并提出质疑。
• 方法的验证和证明：fzysingularity和srameshc希望看到更多关于方法有效性和模型微调的证据。
• 类似工具的比较：yu3zhou4分享了类似工具的开发经验，为Plexe提供了参考。

争议焦点：Plexe能否真正解决ML过程中的核心困难，特别是数据质量评估和特征设计，还是仅限于自动化简单任务。

plexe ✨
Build machine learning models using natural language.
Quickstart
|
Features
|
Installation

Documentation
plexe
lets you create machine learning models by describing them in plain language. Simply explain what you want,
and the AI-powered system builds a fully functional model through an automated agentic approach. Also available as a
managed cloud service
.
demo.mp4
1. Quickstart
Installation
pip install plexe
Using plexe
You can use plexe as a Python library to build and train machine learning models:
import
plexe
# Define the model
model
=
plexe
.
Model
(
intent
=
"Predict sentiment from news articles"
,
input_schema
=
{
"headline"
:
str
,
"content"
:
str
},
output_schema
=
{
"sentiment"
:
str
}
)
# Build and train the model
model
.
build
(
datasets
=
[
your_dataset
],
provider
=
"openai/gpt-4o-mini"
,
max_iterations
=
10
)
# Use the model
prediction
=
model
.
predict
({
"headline"
:
"New breakthrough in renewable energy"
,
"content"
:
"Scientists announced a major advancement..."
})
# Save for later use
plexe
.
save_model
(
model
,
"sentiment-model"
)
loaded_model
=
plexe
.
load_model
(
"sentiment-model.tar.gz"
)
2. Features
2.1. 💬 Natural Language Model Definition
Define models using plain English descriptions:
model
=
plexe
.
Model
(
intent
=
"Predict housing prices based on features like size, location, etc."
,
input_schema
=
{
"square_feet"
:
int
,
"bedrooms"
:
int
,
"location"
:
str
},
output_schema
=
{
"price"
:
float
}
)
2.2. 🤖 Multi-Agent Architecture
The system uses a team of specialized AI agents to:
Analyze your requirements and data
Plan the optimal model solution
Generate and improve model code
Test and evaluate performance
Package the model for deployment
2.3. 🎯 Automated Model Building
Build complete models with a single method call:
model
.
build
(
datasets
=
[
dataset_a
,
dataset_b
],
provider
=
"openai/gpt-4o-mini"
,

=
10
,

=
1800

Plexe supports distributed model training and evaluation with Ray for faster parallel processing:
from
plexe
import

,

model
.

=

)

Use your preferred LLM provider, for example:

data.title: Curl: We still have not seen a valid security report done with AI help
data.author: indigodaddy
data.article_summary: Daniel Stenberg, CEO of curl, 表达了对HackerOne平台上大量低质量AI生成的安全报告的不满。他宣布，将要求每个提交报告的人说明是否使用了AI生成报告，并对被认为是AI粗制滥造的报告提交者立即封禁。Stenberg提到，他们尚未看到任何有效的AI辅助安全报告，且这种现象已接近DDoS攻击的程度。他考虑过通过要求提交者支付保证金来提高报告质量，并对AI生成垃圾报告进行过滤。其他用户也提出了类似的担忧和建议，如建立全球黑名单或白名单，以及利用GPT管道处理报告等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成漏洞报告的有效性及相关问题

不同观点：
• danielvf、parliament32、meindnoch等认为AI生成的漏洞报告大多是无效的，充斥着误导性信息，浪费审查者的时间。他们指出，使用AI的人往往无法区分真实漏洞和虚假信息，导致大量垃圾报告，甚至有人利用AI进行DDoS攻击式的报告提交。
• vessenes、kazinator建议通过建立声誉系统或收取押金的方式来提高报告质量，过滤掉低质量的AI生成报告。他们认为这样可以激励高质量的漏洞报告，并减少垃圾报告的数量。
• ianbutler提供了一个反例，说明AI工具在特定条件下可以找到有效的漏洞，并强调了专业知识在使用这些工具中的重要性。他认为，虽然很多AI生成的报告是无效的，但在专业人士手中，AI工具仍然有其价值。
• GuB-42对AI工具的完全无效性提出质疑，认为需要更深入地研究为什么AI在某些情况下无效，以及如何改进。他指出，curl项目可能由于其高质量和使用传统分析工具而使得AI分析效果不佳。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论者如bogwog、rdtsc提到，利用AI生成大量无效报告可能是一种试图获取关注或经济利益的手段，这进一步加剧了问题的严重性。
• jacksnipe批评了过度依赖AI生成内容的人，认为他们应该理解并验证AI提供的信息，而不是盲目地接受和传播。
• molticrystal提到对LinkedIn等平台的访问限制问题，并提供了一些替代访问的方法，以便让更多人能够查看相关讨论。

争议焦点：
• AI生成漏洞报告的有效性和其对安全研究的影响是讨论的核心。一方认为AI生成报告大多无效且有害，另一方则认为在特定情况下AI可以提供有价值的帮助，但需要专业知识辅助。

43907376.article_summary: Daniel Stenberg, CEO of curl, 表达了对HackerOne平台上大量低质量AI生成的安全报告的不满。他宣布，将要求每个提交报告的人说明是否使用了AI生成报告，并对被认为是AI粗制滥造的报告提交者立即封禁。Stenberg提到，他们尚未看到任何有效的AI辅助安全报告，且这种现象已接近DDoS攻击的程度。他考虑过通过要求提交者支付保证金来提高报告质量，并对AI生成垃圾报告进行过滤。其他用户也提出了类似的担忧和建议，如建立全球黑名单或白名单，以及利用GPT管道处理报告等。
43907376.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成漏洞报告的有效性及相关问题

不同观点：
• danielvf、parliament32、meindnoch等认为AI生成的漏洞报告大多是无效的，充斥着误导性信息，浪费审查者的时间。他们指出，使用AI的人往往无法区分真实漏洞和虚假信息，导致大量垃圾报告，甚至有人利用AI进行DDoS攻击式的报告提交。
• vessenes、kazinator建议通过建立声誉系统或收取押金的方式来提高报告质量，过滤掉低质量的AI生成报告。他们认为这样可以激励高质量的漏洞报告，并减少垃圾报告的数量。
• ianbutler提供了一个反例，说明AI工具在特定条件下可以找到有效的漏洞，并强调了专业知识在使用这些工具中的重要性。他认为，虽然很多AI生成的报告是无效的，但在专业人士手中，AI工具仍然有其价值。
• GuB-42对AI工具的完全无效性提出质疑，认为需要更深入地研究为什么AI在某些情况下无效，以及如何改进。他指出，curl项目可能由于其高质量和使用传统分析工具而使得AI分析效果不佳。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论者如bogwog、rdtsc提到，利用AI生成大量无效报告可能是一种试图获取关注或经济利益的手段，这进一步加剧了问题的严重性。
• jacksnipe批评了过度依赖AI生成内容的人，认为他们应该理解并验证AI提供的信息，而不是盲目地接受和传播。
• molticrystal提到对LinkedIn等平台的访问限制问题，并提供了一些替代访问的方法，以便让更多人能够查看相关讨论。

争议焦点：
• AI生成漏洞报告的有效性和其对安全研究的影响是讨论的核心。一方认为AI生成报告大多无效且有害，另一方则认为在特定情况下AI可以提供有价值的帮助，但需要专业知识辅助。

data.title: Is Planet Nine Alone in the Outer System?
data.author: JPLeRouzic
data.article_summary:
文章探讨了假设存在的第九行星及其在太阳系外围的探索潜力。作者引用Robert Browning的名言，引出人类探索太空边界的渴望，并提到目前对太阳引力透镜距离（约550 AU）的探索。尽管这一目标超出当前技术能力，但JPL的团队正在进行相关任务设计。文章指出，寻找如第九行星这样的新目标可能激发更多探索兴趣，尤其是如果它类似于在其他星系中发现的超级地球或迷你海王星。

研究显示，许多恒星系统存在超级地球，这支持了第九行星存在的可能性。其质量预计为地球的10倍以上，半长轴约700 AU。尽管光学调查未能发现，但通过比较IRAS和AKARI卫星23年间的数据，研究团队尝试寻找可能的红外源，以确认第九行星的存在。文章强调，尽管技术挑战大，但发现新行星将极大推动太空探索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：太阳系外围存在未知大天体（如假想的第九行星或其它大质量天体）的可能性及其相关证据和理论

不同观点：
• adrian_b: 认为许多跨海王星天体的奇特轨道并不能直接证明当前存在一个未发现的大行星。他引用了2024年发表的论文，提出可能是过去有恒星靠近太阳系，导致这些轨道的异常，这种解释比未发现的大行星更可信。
• yellowapple: 主要关注冥王星降级的问题，认为这是对冥王星的不尊重，并开玩笑说不能把假想的跨冥王星天体称为"X行星"。
• Qem: 引用了Brown的观点，认为目前观测到的轨道异常可能无法用"第九行星"假说来解释，并提到Lykawka和Mukai提出的另一个独立的大质量天体假说，可能与Brown和Batygin的假说不兼容。Qem还提出可能存在两个独立的天体影响外太阳系。
• RajT88: 幽默地希望如果发现新的天体，不要长得像一个"8号球"。
• Hobadee: 半开玩笑地认为第九行星就是冥王星，表现出对冥王星是行星的坚持。
• xhrpost: 讨论了利用暗能量相机（DECam）进行后续观测的可能性，并尝试计算在特定距离上的分辨率，以评估发现小天体的可行性。
• glimshe: 抱怨网站劫持滚动条的行为，与主要讨论点无关。
• cratermoon: 认为冥王星是众多跨海王星天体中最大的一个，暗示没有必要引入新的行星假说。
• eth0up: 开玩笑地认为未知天体可能是一个小黑洞。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是太阳系外围奇特轨道的成因。adrian_b支持恒星经过假说，而Qem则引用了不同的大质量天体假说，并探讨了多个天体共同作用的可能性。
• 冥王星的地位问题虽然以幽默形式出现，但也反映了部分讨论者对冥王星作为行星的深厚情感。
• 一些讨论者如xhrpost更关注技术细节，如利用现有设备进行观测的可行性，显示了讨论的技术性一面。
• 其他如glimshe的评论属于对网页体验的抱怨，与科学讨论无直接关系。

43907586.article_content:
Is Planet Nine Alone in the Outer System?
by
Paul Gilster
|
May 6, 2025
|
Outer Solar System
|
2 comments
It was Robert Browning who said “Ah, but a man’s reach should exceed his grasp, or what’s a heaven for?” A rousing thought, but we don’t always know where we should reach. In terms of space exploration, a distant but feasible target is the solar gravitational lens distance beginning around 550 AU. So far the SGL definitely exceeds our grasp, but solid work in mission design by Slava Turyshev and team is ongoing at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory.
Targets need to tantalize, and maybe a target that we hadn’t previously considered is now emerging. Planet Nine, the hypothesized world that may lurk somewhere in our Solar System’s outer reaches, would be such an extraordinary discovery that it would tempt future mission designers in the same way.
This is interesting because right now our deep space targets need to be well defined. I love the idea of
Interstellar Probe
, the craft designed at JHU/APL, but it’s hard to excite the public with the idea of looking back at the heliosphere from the outside (although the science return would be fabulous). Pluto was hard enough to sell to the powers that be, but Allen Stern and team got the job done because they had a whole world that had never been seen up close. Will Planet Nine, if found, turn out to be the destination that some budget-strapped team finds a way to explore?
We have a lot to learn about planetary demographics given that our planet-finding technologies work best for larger worlds closer in to their stars. But a recent microlensing study suggests that as many as one out of every three stars in our galaxy should host a super-Earth in a Jupiter-like orbit (citation below). Microlensing is helpful because it can reveal planets at large distances from their parent stars. Super-Earths appear to be abundant. If it exists, Planet Nine isn’t in a Jovian orbit, but it’s probably smaller than Neptune.
In so many ways this planet makes sense. We’ve found planets like it in innumerable stellar systems. We also know that mechanisms of gravitational slingshotting can push a planet either out of its system entirely or into an entirely new orbit, explaining our prior lack of detection. We’re talking about a planet on the order of a super-Earth or a mini-Neptune, the former larger than our planet but still rocky, the latter smaller than Neptune but gaseous.
Image:
An illustration shows what Planet Nine might look like orbiting far from our Sun. We have found many such worlds around other stars, but finding one in our own backyard is taking time because of its distance and an orbit that is probably well off the ecliptic. Assuming a planet is there at all. Image credit: NASA/Caltech.
The evidence in the orbits of a number of outer system objects points to something perturbing their paths, and seems to implicate something big. Now we have, after years of evidence gathering and debate, at least a possible candidate for this world. In process at
Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia (PASA)
, although not yet published, the paper digs deep into data from the Infrared Astronomical Satellite as well as AKARI, a Japanese satellite somewhat more sensitive than IRAS and launched in 2006.
The distant Sedna and other similar bodies with unusual orbital characteristics tell us that something has to account for their high eccentricity and inclination, while a number of Kuiper Belt objects seem to be similarly affected, as shown in the orientation of their orbits (described through what is known as the
argument of perihelion
). Computations thus far indicate mass on the order of something equal to or greater than 10 Earth masses, with a semi-major axis of about 700 AU.
Image:
The six most distant known objects in the solar system with orbits exclusively beyond Neptune (magenta) all mysteriously line up in a single direction. Moreover, when viewed in 3-D, the orbits of all these icy little objects are tilted in the same direction, away from the plane of the solar system. PL-Caltech/R. Hurt.
A huge amount of work has gone into this analysis, all ably summarized in the paper, which comes from Terry Long Phan (National Tsing Hua University, Taiwan) and colleagues. Optical surveys have heretofore failed to find this object, but 700 AU is fully 23 times the distance of Neptune from the Sun, far enough out that visible wavelengths need to give way to infrared to find it.
Phan’s team looked for candidate objects in the range of 500 to 700 AU using the two far-infrared surveys mentioned above, which are both all-sky in range but separated by 23 years, making for useful comparisons. The idea was to find an object that moved from an IRAS position to an AKARI position after those 23 years. data.title: Show HN: Reverse Pac-Man
data.author: Eagle64
data.article_summary:
"Reverse Pac-Man"是一款与经典《吃豆人》玩法相反的游戏。玩家控制幽灵去捕捉Pac-Man，而非传统中Pac-Man吃豆并躲避幽灵。具体操作如下：  
- 红色幽灵（Ghost 1）：使用WASD或ZQSD键控制移动。  
- 青色幽灵（Ghost 2）：使用方向键控制移动。  

游戏通过反转角色控制，带来新的挑战和乐趣。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对游戏机制、功能和体验的反馈与建议

不同观点：
• [tantalor] 认为当前的方向改变机制过于严苛，建议允许玩家在到达路口之前按住按键来改变方向，以提高可玩性。当前的机制要求在非常短的时间窗口内按键，使得游戏变得困难。
• [KennedyHere] 对游戏的期待与实际体验不同，原本以为是要引导Pac-Man把所有点放回原位，表明游戏标题可能引起误解。
• [amadeuspagel] 赞赏游戏控制两个角色的创意，建议通过颜色区分箭头键和WASD键的控制说明，以增强用户体验。
• [brudgers] 提到在笔记本电脑上无法看到整个屏幕，且屏幕不滚动，影响了游戏体验。
• [adamiscool8] 对计分机制有疑问，不确定是否应该倒计时，还是通过吃掉更多目标来获得高分。

补充讨论：
• [narcindin] 提到一个类似的老游戏《swap box turbo》，具有双人控制机制，表明这种玩法并非全新概念，并提供了参考链接。
• [bentcorner] 推荐了另一个具有相似玩法的游戏《Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons》，建议玩家体验，并提供了购买链接。
• [kazinator] 确认了tantalor的观点，认为幽灵在路口前不响应按键可能是设计上的故意安排，但依然感到困扰。
• [xnx] 建议增加双摇杆控制器支持，并提供了技术文档链接。
• [mtVessel] 和 [progforlyfe] 都遇到了游戏加载问题，分别报告了安全连接失败和游戏无法加载的问题。
• [roskelld] 建议加入能量药丸机制，让Pac-Man有更多对抗机会，并指出游戏开始时角色在左上角无意义绕圈的bug。
• [iorekz] 简单地赞赏了游戏的创意，没有提出具体建议或问题。

争议焦点：
• 游戏的方向控制机制是否过于严苛，影响玩家体验。
• 计分机制的设定是否合理，玩家对其理解存在分歧。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 游戏的加载问题和技术故障报告。
• 对游戏玩法和类似游戏的参考与推荐。
• 对游戏中角色行为bug的反馈。

• [kazinator] 确认了tantalor的观点，认为幽灵在路口前不响应按键可能是设计上的故意安排，但依然感到困扰。
• [xnx] 建议增加双摇杆控制器支持，并提供了技术文档链接。
• [mtVessel] 和 [progforlyfe] 都遇到了游戏加载问题，分别报告了安全连接失败和游戏无法加载的问题。
• [roskelld] 建议加入能量药丸机制，让Pac-Man有更多对抗机会，并指出游戏开始时角色在左上角无意义绕圈的bug。
• [iorekz] 简单地赞赏了游戏的创意，没有提出具体建议或问题。

争议焦点：
• 游戏的方向控制机制是否过于严苛，影响玩家体验。
• 计分机制的设定是否合理，玩家对其理解存在分歧。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 游戏的加载问题和技术故障报告。
• 对游戏玩法和类似游戏的参考与推荐。
• 对游戏中角色行为bug的反馈。

data.title: DoomArena: A Framework for Testing AI Agents Against Evolving Security Threats
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一个名为DoomArena的框架，用于测试AI代理面对不断演变的安全威胁。该框架基于三个原则：可插拔设计，易于集成到实际代理框架中；可配置，支持详细的威胁建模；模块化，攻击开发与环境细节解耦，允许跨多个环境应用相同攻击。DoomArena具有适应新威胁模型和环境、结合多种攻击进行全面安全测试、分析漏洞与性能权衡等优势。实验显示，当前最先进的（SOTA）网络和工具调用代理对不同威胁模型的脆弱性各异，基于强大SOTA LLM的防御效果更佳。DoomArena代码已开源。

Title:
DoomArena: A framework for Testing AI Agents Against Evolving Security Threats
Authors:

View a PDF of the paper titled DoomArena: A framework for Testing AI Agents Against Evolving Security Threats, by Leo Boisvert and 11 other authors
View PDF
Abstract:
We present DoomArena, a security evaluation framework for AI agents. DoomArena is designed on three principles: 1) It is a plug-in framework and integrates easily into realistic agentic frameworks like BrowserGym (for web agents) and $\tau$-bench (for tool calling agents); 2) It is configurable and allows for detailed threat modeling, allowing configuration of specific components of the agentic framework being attackable, and specifying targets for the attacker; and 3) It is modular and decouples the development of attacks from details of the environment in which the agent is deployed, allowing for the same attacks to be applied across multiple environments. We illustrate several advantages of our framework, including the ability to adapt to new threat models and environments easily, the ability to easily combine several previously published attacks to enable comprehensive and fine-grained security testing, and the ability to analyze trade-offs between various vulnerabilities and performance. We apply DoomArena to state-of-the-art (SOTA) web and tool-calling agents and find a number of surprising results: 1) SOTA agents have varying levels of vulnerability to different threat models (malicious user vs malicious environment), and there is no Pareto dominant agent across all threat models; 2) When multiple attacks are applied to an agent, they often combine constructively; 3) Guardrail model-based defenses seem to fail, while defenses based on powerful SOTA LLMs work better. DoomArena is available at

data.title: Free with In-App Purchase is a sham
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文批评了苹果App Store中“免费+内购”应用程序的误导性标签，指出其定义模糊，容易让消费者混淆。作者认为，苹果所谓的“免费”仅指下载时无需付费，但并未清楚说明使用应用时可能需要的付费内容，导致不同应用的内购范围和限制差异巨大。一些应用甚至在下载后无法使用，除非用户先支付内购费用，而苹果对这种“诱导转换”策略并无明显反对。作者举例说明某款排名靠前的应用存在误导性定价和不透明的取消订阅指引，批评苹果的审核团队未能有效保护消费者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：应用商店中的“免费+内购”模式及其优缺点

不同观点：
• [hedora的观点] 认为文章中提到的问题源于App Store的筛选不力，而不是“免费+内购”模式本身。他提到自己使用一些免费但包含内购的应用程序，并没有遇到问题。
• [AStoneThrow的观点] 基于Google Play商店的体验，指出“免费+内购”模式在实际使用中可能会变得混乱，尤其是在多个设备和账户之间切换时，容易导致用户对已购买内容的混淆。他还提到，对于不熟悉的应用，用户希望先试用再决定是否购买，而“免费+内购”模式在这种情况下更为合适。同时，他也承认有些开发者可能故意让用户混淆，从而让用户重复付费。
• [dlachausse的观点] 认为“免费+内购”模式利用了消费者的心理，他们更倾向于选择免费的应用，并逐步被引导进行内购消费。虽然一次性付费可能对用户更有利，但这种模式难以与“免费”应用竞争。

补充讨论：
• 一些应用提供两种版本，一个是直接付费的“高级版”，另一个是免费但包含内购的“试用版”，这种双重列表可能会导致用户混淆，尤其是在多个设备和账户之间切换时。
• AStoneThrow提到，某些应用通过辅助应用（如“Supporter”应用）来解锁主应用的高级功能，这种做法虽然解决了某些问题，但也增加了用户的困惑。
• dlachausse指出，消费者往往被“免费”标签吸引，即使最终可能在内购上花费更多，这种心理倾向使得“免费+内购”模式在市场上更具竞争力。

争议焦点：
• “免费+内购”模式是否是必要的，还是由于应用商店机制不完善导致的。
• 用户在使用“免费+内购”模式时，是否因混淆而导致重复付费，这是否是开发者的有意设计。

43907763.article_content:
Free with In-App Purchase is a sham
May 6 2025
A couple of weeks ago I published a blog post about
App Store Curation
. At the end I said:
Apple claims that locking down iOS to the App Store is justified in order to protect consumers from danger. Time and again, however, it's painfully obvious that Apple's so-called "curation" of the App Store is terrible, miserable, incompetent, negligent.
By the way, the app I wrote about,
Virus Protection for Phone
, was removed from the App Store shortly thereafter. Perhaps Apple should pay me to do their job for them. How about a bounty for scams? I'll take, say, 30% of their revenue.
In this blog post, I want to discuss a fundamental, intentional design flaw of the App Store that misleads consumers: the category of apps that are labeled as free with In-App Purchase. The App Store shows an explanation of In-App Purchases when you click the Learn More link in the In-App Purchases section of an app's product page; here's a quote from the first paragraph of Apple's document:
Many of your favorite free and paid apps and games offer in-app purchases, which are optional transactions that change an app's functionality or unlock digital goods, content or services. You can find out if an app offers in-app purchases by visiting its product page in the App Store. Just look for the "In-App Purchases" messages near the Get or Price button.
The problem is that what Apple means here by "free" as opposed to "paid" is simply that you don't have to pay before downloading the app, but Apple's counterintuitive definition tends to obscure what is most important to consumers: how much you have to pay to
use
the app. The range of allowed use can vary drastically among apps that are free with IAP. Some apps can be used forever for free with no apparent limitations, and the IAP merely unlocks bonus content or features. Some can be used for free in "reader" mode, with the ability to open and read documents, while an IAP is required to edit and/or sync documents. Some apps are free to use fully for only a limited time; in other words, they have a time-limited free trial. At the end of the trial, various outcomes are possible. Time-limited trials are especially popular with auto-renewing subscription apps, which start charging you automatically at the end of the trial. And ironically, some so-called "free" apps don't allow any use at all unless you first pay the IAP.
Three years ago,
I highlighted such an app
that was free to download but could not be used in any way without the IAP. In response to the ensuing negative publicity, the developer of the app added a time-limited free trial. Nonetheless, Apple had already approved the app without a free trial, and there's no evidence that Apple or its app review team has any objection to the bait-and-switch tactic. As
Nick Heer wrote at the time:
This is the kind of thing Apple sought to prevent when it launched In-App Purchases as a
feature for paid apps only
. Opening them up to free apps has created different purchasing mechanisms in the App Store and has pushed the industry toward subscription pricing, but it has also enabled scummy behaviour like this.
The app in question is still
in the Mac App Store
, apparently renamed from "Docs Pro for Google Drive" to "Docs for Google Docs and Drive", but still labeled as free with IAP. In fact it's one of the Mac App Store's most financially successful apps, currently ranked #33 top grossing the United States,
according to AppFigures
.
Below is a screenshot of the app's window now on first launch (click to see full size):
You might be shocked to learn that the window is actually
floating
. That is, it floats above and covers every other window on the Mac, even if you switch to a different app. And Apple approved this. You can close the floating window, but that quits the app.
By default, the lifetime $39.99 license is selected. It's labeled "Best choice - no subscription". The 3 day free trial is available only if you select the $19.99 yearly subscription option. The subtitle of the subscription option says, "Only $5.00/month", the math of which is
way
off and would add up to $60 per year if accurate. I don't know how that window got approved by Apple.
To get the free trial, I selected the subscription option.
The instructions for canceling the trial are vague, "in your account". This may be unhelpful or even confusing for novice App Store users, the very people most in need of Apple's protection. Adding to the potential confusion, as soon as you press OK, a new window opens asking you to Sign in to Google with your Google account. (I'll present evidence of customer confusion later in this blog post, in the form of App Store user reviews.)
Fortunately, I did receive a subscription confirmation email from Apple that included a link to my Apple Account subscriptions management page and confirmed the terms of the subscription: "To avoid being charged, you must cancel at least a day before each billing date."

data.title: Instant (YC S22) Is Hiring a Founding TypeScript Engineer
data.author: stopachka
data.article_summary: Instant 是一个结合了 Firebase 和 Supabase 优点的实时数据库，支持关系同步。其团队正在寻找一位创始 TypeScript 工程师，要求对类型设计有极致追求，能够提升开发者体验，并帮助构建类似 Figma 或 Notion 的同步引擎。团队希望优化类型的智能提示和性能，例如通过自动补全和类型安全改善查询体验，并提升 CLI 和 Dashboard 的用户界面，使其更直观和高效。此外，团队还计划改进迁移支持、沙盒功能和数据浏览器，以打造更完善的开发者工具。

43897138.article_content:
instant
instant
Founding Typescript Engineer
Instant is a real-time database you can use on the frontend. We give you the best of both Firebase and Supabase, a sync-engine with support for relations. This is the kind of tech that companies like Figma, Notion, and Linear build internally to power their products (
Try out the demo
)
We're looking for a founding Typescript Engineer to join our team of 4 in San Francisco. If you:
Are obsessive about type ergonomics (even with how types show up in intellisense)
Enjoy crafting UIs that people use for hours
Want to build a sync engine to enable the next Figma or Notion
Then we want to talk to you! So, why those three points? Let us explain:
1
.
You are obsessive about type ergonomics
One of the benefits about using typescript in a library is the developer experience you can offer your users. Types can do so much more than just catch typos. Types are a tool. They give you autocomplete and good feedback; shown in the right moment they can make someone's day. We don't just want to build a great database. We want people to enjoy using it.
Instant is
typed
. It took some serious
type fu

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Kubernetes配置管理工具的选择与使用

不同观点：
• atmosx认为Kustomize在大规模管理时更易用，但需要前期投入。他提到许多图表作为Helm包分发，因此需要导出为YAML。他建议结合ArgoCD使用Kustomize，但在需要动态替换变量时可能需要使用envsubst。

• arccy表示如果只处理自己的项目，可以避免使用Helm，他推荐使用CUE生成Kubernetes YAML。他提到如果需要类似Helm的体验但使用CUE，可以考虑Timoni。他还指出，处理上游项目时，可能不得不使用Helm或重写它们。

• haiku2077使用ArgoCD处理简单任务，对于复杂任务则编写Python或Go程序生成清单，然后使用kubectl应用。

• b11484提到正在改进一个使用Jsonnet的工具kr8+，用于组合集群配置并应用到组件。

• bithavoc使用Pulumi的原生包进行Kubernetes管理，完全避免YAML，只使用TypeScript类实例。

• dvektor不喜欢将Git仓库作为Helm图表，但同时也认为不使用Helm而手写各种YAML文件更糟糕。

• Nerudite推荐Helmsman工具，提供了一个GitHub链接。

• Vespasian推荐使用fluxcd进行GitOps工作流，并提到其整合了处理秘密信息的soap。

• LarsLarson分享了他们使用Kustomize创建YAML并用ArgoCD进行部署的经验，通过CI和GitOps工作良好。

• natbennett偏好使用ytt进行模板处理，使用kapp进行部署，提供了一个Carvel项目的链接。

• delduca表示支持使用Kustomize。

• johnjungles简单表示支持ArgoCD。

补充讨论：
- 讨论涉及多种工具的比较和选择，如Kustomize、Helm、CUE、Pulumi、ArgoCD、fluxcd、ytt、kapp等。
- 不同工具的优缺点和适用场景被多次提到，例如Helm在处理上游项目时的必要性与麻烦，以及Kustomize在动态配置和管理上的优势。
- 争议焦点在于是否使用Helm及其图表，以及如何有效管理Kubernetes配置以满足不同工作流需求。

data.author: cenazoic
data.article_summary: 《Coconut Action Party》是一本由Lin Yangchen撰写的 comprehensive 著作，涵盖与椰子主题相关的邮票设计、印刷技术、历史背景及防伪特征等。书中探讨了椰子主题邮票的演变、不同地区如马来西亚、新加坡等地的设计差异，以及二战前后的邮票历史。书中还详细介绍了印刷工艺、纸张分析、油墨颜色、伪造邮票的鉴别以及各种科学分析方法，如光谱学和显微技术。附录提供了椰子邮票的稀有度图表和百科知识。该书内容广泛，涉及邮票收藏的多个方面，适合 philatelists（集邮爱好者）及历史研究者阅读。

data.title: Technical analysis of the Signal clone used by Trump officials
data.author: micahflee
data.article_summary: 本文披露了特朗普政府官员使用的一款非官方Signal克隆应用——TM SGNL，该应用由TeleMessage公司开发，能够自动存档明文消息，甚至包括那些设置为阅后即焚的消息。TM SGNL利用Signal的服务器进行端到端加密通讯，但会将聊天记录存档到其他可能不安全的地方，如Gmail账户。该应用疑似违反了Signal的开源许可证，且未公开提供下载，仅通过企业设备管理服务分发。TeleMessage公司高管多有以色列国防军情报部门的背景，其行为可能涉及违规使用Signal及其他软件的专有许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Signal加密通信系统的安全性及其在政府和特朗普行政部门的应用

不同观点：
• [tomhow] 和 [abhisek] 提到了将Signal等端到端加密消息存档到可能破坏其安全模型的存储系统中的矛盾。abhisek特别质疑这种做法是否违背了使用Signal的初衷，即为了安全和隐私。
• [cycomanic] 和 [mdhb] 提到了Telemessage应用的漏洞以及其与外国情报机构的关系。cycomanic指出Telemessage已经被黑客攻击，而mdhb则关注该应用由前以色列情报官员控制，暗示可能存在安全隐患。
• [ComputerGuru] 和 [ThinkBeat] 讨论了政府官员使用Signal的合法性以及是否存在由美国军方或NSA开发的专用安全通信工具。ComputerGuru特别质疑Telemessage是否得到了官方批准，而ThinkBeat则推测是否存在一个结合硬件和软件的专用通信系统。
• [egberts1] 和 [throw7] 关心TM SGNL（Telemessage的Signal克隆版）是否被Signal官方允许连接到Signal网络，以及其安全性是否会因此受损。throw7特别质疑Signal是否允许非官方版本的应用连接到其网络。
• [mmooss] 和 [lrvick] 深入讨论了使用非官方客户端（如TM SGNL）可能导致的安全漏洞，尤其是消息存档和删除策略的不一致。mmooss担心用户使用非官方客户端会破坏Signal的安全保证，而lrvick提出了一种技术方案来实现消息存档的同时保持端到端加密。

补充讨论：
• [gbraad] 指出，由于没有对实际二进制文件进行技术分析，因此无法确定应用是否被修改。这种分析依赖于文档和分配过程。
• [be_erik] 认为，虽然不希望政府官员使用Signal，但Signal本身是一个优秀的安全通信工具。
• [jimmydoe] 讽刺地评论了特朗普行政部门遵循法律存档聊天记录的做法，并批评了Telemessage的技术 incompetence。
• [ThinkBeat] 提到政府官员使用“工作”和“私人”手机的做法，工作手机通常经过加固并使用安全的政府VPN系统。

争议焦点：
• 是否应将端到端加密的消息存档，特别是当存档过程可能破坏其加密安全性时。
• Telemessage等第三方应用是否得到了适当的批准和审查，尤其是考虑到其潜在的安全隐患和与外国情报机构的关系。
• Signal是否应对非官方客户端进行标识，以确保用户通信的安全性和隐私性。

43875476.article_content:
💡
Update May 3, 2025:
I have posted a follow-up,
Here's the source code for the unofficial Signal app used by Trump officials
.
Update May 4, 2025:
Another followup, and a big one:
The Signal Clone the Trump Admin Uses Was Hacked
Yesterday, a Reuters photographer captured a
photo
of the freshly-ousted former National Security Advisor Mike Waltz checking his Signal messages during a Trump cabinet meeting. If you're not familiar with Waltz, he's most well known for inviting The Atlantic's editor-in-chief to secret Trump administration
war crimes Signal group
. They discussed, and executed, bombing an urban apartment building full of civilians to kill a single man.
404 Media journalist Joseph Cox
published a story
pointing out that Waltz was not using the official Signal app, but rather "an obscure and unofficial version of Signal that is designed to archive messages" called TM SGNL.
Zoomed-in crop of the Reuters photo showing Mike Waltz using the TM SGNL app. Images credit: REUTERS/Evelyn Hockstein
This app uses Signal's servers, making it possible for Waltz to send end-to-end encrypted messages to normal Signal users, like Jeffrey Goldberg from The Atlantic, for example. However unlike the Signal end of the encrypted conversation, the TM SGNL end automatically archives a copy of the plaintext messages (even ones with disappearing messages) somewhere else that may or may not be secure.
In a
video
the company published, they show Signal messages getting archived into a Gmail account.
I decided to look into this app. I discovered:
The senior executives of the company behind TM SGNL appear to be Israeli, and the CEO's bio mentions his work with Israel Defense Forces' Intelligence unit.
TM SGNL is most likely violating Signal's open source license, and the company's other apps are probably violating the proprietary licenses of other software like WhatsApp and WeChat.
The Android and iOS versions of the app are not available for the public to download, and in fact practically the only way to get the app is if you're using a device enrolled in an MDM service that's tied to an Apple Business Manager or Google Enterprise account.
I speculate about exactly how I think the Trump administration is using this (unapproved for classified info) app to discuss classified info, and how they are likely managing their fleet of iPhones.
Finally, I share a PDF and a video I discovered that go into detail about, among other things, where the chat logs may be stored.
Before I get started, consider
subscribing
to get these posts emailed directly to your inbox. If you want to support my work, considering becoming a paid supporter.
The company behind TM SGNL
The TM SGNL app is part of a suite of apps by a company called
TeleMessage
, which is owned by
Smarsh
, a company that makes e-discovery software, which is basically software designed for police and lawyers and whatnot to search archives of data.
I haven't spent a lot of time looking into TeleMessage, but what I did find at a quick glance is that several of the executives on the
teams page
list Israeli universities in their bios, and the CEO, Guy Levit, says that, "From 1996 until 1999, Guy served as the head of the planning and development of one of the IDF’s Intelligence elite technical units."
How the app probably works
Based on the photo of Waltz's screen, TM SGNL is most likely a version of Signal that is slightly modified. The app name is changed from "Signal" to "TM SGNL" (which is why Walt'z screen says, "Verify your TM SGNL PIN" instead of "Verify your Signal PIN").
And there is most likely an additional piece of code that gets executed whenever a message is sent or received which forwards the plaintext version of that message to the "corporate archive," as the company calls it.
TM SGNL might be violating Signal's open source licenses
Signal is open source. Here's the
Signal-iOS
code and here's the
Signal-Android
code. Because the code is available, creating an app like TM SGNL would actually be pretty easy to do.
Signal has done all of the hard work in making an end-to-end encryption messaging app. Signal also runs the server infrastructure. The TeleMessage devs simply have to clone the git repos of the client apps, figure out where to insert the archiving code, and make their own separate releases.
The Signal apps are licensed under the
GNU Affero General Public License
, a copyleft license that allows anyone to make modified versions (like TM SGNL) provided that they also use the same open source license. The license text says that when making modifications to the source code:
You must license the entire work, as a whole, under this License to anyone who comes into possession of a copy.
So, if someone has a copy of TM SGNL, they should be able to request that TeleMessage provide a copy of the source code, which should also be open source, and if TeleMessage does not comply they will be violating Signal's license – essentially, selling pirated software.

data.author: isolli
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了智能手机和社交媒体对人们精神、社交、认知和道德方面的负面影响，特别是它们如何剥夺了人们的无聊时刻和间隙时间，而这些时间原本是用于白日梦和自我反思的。作者Christine Rosen指出，随着手机成为生活的主要部分，人们失去了安静沉思的机会，导致创造力和人性的衰退。文章引用了Jon Haidt的观点，强调持续的刺激和即时满足正侵蚀着我们的耐心和深度思考能力，呼吁保护这些间隙时间以维持我们的创造力和人性。智能手机虽然消除了无聊，但也带来了诸如焦虑、孤独和抑郁等负面影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：智能手机和数字设备对人们心理状态、创造力和自我反思的影响，以及如何有效管理设备使用时间。

不同观点：
• **支持减少智能手机使用，提倡“无聊”时间**：
  - [elbasti] 通过使用非智能手机，强迫自己面对困难决策，减少了焦虑和拖延。
  - [tines] 通过减少智能手机使用，恢复了“无聊”时间，认为这对精神健康至关重要。
  - [gaoshan] 意识到智能手机消耗时间，特别是通过社交媒体和无意识的浏览。
  - [susam] 依赖物理工具（如书本和纸张）和自我控制（如屏蔽分心网站）来保持专注和创造力。
  - [codyb] 避免无限滚动的产品，通过远离手机促进健康和创造力。
  - [entropie] 每天不使用手机的长时间散步帮助反思和决策。
  - [hs586] 认为无聊是一种奢侈，是深度思考和自我反思的机会。

• **强调适度使用和平衡**：
  - [bhouston] 认为白日梦和反思是策略性思考的重要部分，但需要在行动和反思之间找到平衡。
  - [forcer] 反思过度专注于某项事业（如创业）可能导致对其他生活记忆的忽视，强调平衡的重要性。
  - [chiefgeek] 强调平衡，完全脱离社交媒体带来了显著的体验，但也强调适度使用和自我调节。

• **对“无聊”和设备使用的不同看法**：
  - [theletterf] 认为每个人都有权决定如何分配自己的注意力和时间，不应被强迫脱离手机。
  - [spudlyo] 认为在有限时间内不想浪费时间在“无聊”上，理解人们依赖手机打发时间。

• **对白日梦的潜在负面影响**：
  - [hirvi74] 提出白日梦可能是有害的，特别是当它成为一种逃避行动的捷径时，强调适度的重要性。

补充讨论：
- 不同方法和工具（如乐高、散步、物理书本）被用来促进反思和创造力。
- 对智能手机和社交媒体成瘾的个人体验和应对策略，如使用技术手段（脚本、屏蔽网站）来管理分心。
- 不同背景和生活经历（如乡村生活、创业经历）对设备使用和心理状态的影响。

争议焦点：
- 是否应该强迫自己或他人减少智能手机使用以促进反思和创造力，还是尊重个人选择和生活方式。
- 白日梦的潜在负面影响与它对创造力和反思的积极作用之间的平衡。

On The Death of Daydreaming
What we lose when phones take away boredom and interstitial time
Christine Rosen
May 05, 2025
341

Intro from Jon Haidt:
When I was nearly finished writing
The Anxious Generation
in the summer of 2023, I realized that I had left a gap. The book focused on the collapse of mental health, attention, and socialization of Gen Z—but again and again, older readers and friends would tell me: “this is happening to me too.” I realized that the global transition to a phone-based life is transforming
everyone’s
consciousness. But how? What exactly is happening to us?
I thought back to my first book,
The Happiness Hypothesis
, which explored ten ancient ideas about how to live a good life—ideas found across continents and millennia. I began to see that the phone-based life, and social media in particular, push us to live in ways that are directly contrary to those recommended by nearly every ancient religious and philosophical tradition. These traditions tell us to be
slow to judge
and
quick to forgive
. They offer practices like meditation to quiet the mind and open the heart to deeper truths and greater communion.
In
The Anxious Generation
, I explored six of these contradictions in Chapter 8. A simple summary of that chapter is this: the phone-based life diminishes our humanity. Compared to the life we once lived, it degrades us morally, spiritually, socially, and cognitively.
Since writing that chapter, I’vebeen on the lookout for others who can express this loss of humanity better than I can. Here’s my short list: L.M. Sacasas for his Substack
The Convivial Society
; Nicholas Carr, for
The Shallows
and his more recent book
Superbloom
; and Christine Rosen, for her 2024 book
The Extinction of Experience
.
(For a Gen Z perspective, see
Freya India
—especially the post we co-wrote
“On The Degrading Effects of Life Online.”)
Today’s post is by Christine Rosen. Christine holds a Ph.D. in history with a focus on American intellectual history. She is
a senior fellow at AEI
, and she was
my discussion partner
when I gave a talk on
The Anxious Generation
at AEI soon after the book launched. That was when I learned about her book project,
The Extinction of Experience: Being Human in a Disembodied World.
Cover of
The Extinction of Experience.
So when her publisher invited me to consider reading an early draft and offering an endorsement, I was glad to say yes. I loved the book, and I hope the blurb I wrote captures its urgency and depth:
Rosen shows us that we are embodied creatures who are rapidly losing the analog world in which our bodies and minds evolved. She shows us that many of the technologically aided advances in convenience and efficiency exact a cost in our humanity, our civility, and ultimately our ability to live together in a democratic society. This is an extremely important book; its message is all the more urgent as AI threatens to make everything effortless and frictionless.
I invited Christine to present a section or idea from her book for
After Babel
. She chose one of my favorites: the loss of “interstitial time.” Interstices are the gaps between things, as with the cells in your body or the spaces between architectural columns. When applied to time, it means the many bits of time scattered throughout the day such as the five minutes that students have in between classes, or the unknown number of seconds that pass while you are waiting for an elevator. These moments used to be given over to silent reflection or conversation with whoever is around. Now, for most of us, nearly all of them are grabbed by our phones.
Christine traces out the profound consequences of losing those interstitial moments, for our creativity and for our humanity. She shows why it is so important to guard those moments for daydreaming.
— Jon

On The Death of Daydreaming
By Christine Rosen
Source: Shutterstock
Can you remember the last time you daydreamed? Or coped with boredom without reaching for your phone? Before the era of mobile technology, most of us had no choice but to wait without stimulation, and often, that meant being bored.
But today we need never be bored. We have an indefatigable boredom-killing machine: the smartphone. No matter how brief our wait, the smartphone promises an alleviation for our suffering.
Yet the smartphone’s triumph over boredom might prove a Pyrrhic victory. As Jonathan Haidt showed in
The Anxious Generation
, the rapid adoption of smartphones and social media, particularly by the young, led to many negative unintended consequences such as increased rates of depression, anxiety, loneliness, and self-harm. data.title: AWS Built a Security Tool. It Introduced a Security Risk
data.author: simplesort
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了AWS的一个安全工具“Account Assessment for AWS Organizations”如何意外引入安全风险。该工具旨在审核跨账户访问的资源策略，但由于部署指引不当，可能导致权限提升风险。具体来说，AWS建议将工具部署在较低敏感性的账户中，使得不安全的账户能够访问高度敏感的账户，从而引发风险。

在一次调查中，研究人员发现某客户环境中存在严重权限提升风险，攻击者可通过开发账户中的角色获取生产和管理账户的敏感权限。进一步调查显示，这一问题源于AWS自身的工具部署指引不当，该工具采用中心辐射型架构，允许中心角色跨账户聚合安全数据，但未明确部署在非管理账户的安全隐患。

AWS已修复此问题，建议受影响组织检查并纠正不当的角色信任关系，以降低风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AWS环境中的安全风险及其处理方式

不同观点：
• yfiapo：认为该问题是一个中等严重性的安全问题，虽然被适当处理，但过度夸大这种较小的问题对任何人都没有帮助。问题在于AWS文档没有明确指出最佳实践，而不是AWS本身推荐不安全的设置。
• placardloop：不认为列出元数据（如秘密名称、存储桶名称等）是安全问题，因为这些List* API不提供对对象本身的访问权限，只是元数据。
• 18172828286177：认为是部署解决方案的人员 incompetence 导致的，不应该在开发账户中部署具有所有账户访问权限的解决方案。
• dangus：比较AWS和Google Cloud，指出AWS的多账户系统复杂，而Google Cloud的文件夹和项目系统更灵活，IAM控制更好。
• atoav：通过城堡的类比说明安全解决方案中的一个根本问题，即给予接触“敌人”的部分系统过多的权限可能会导致整个系统的崩溃。
• swisniewski：强烈反对文章的观点，认为AWS模型简单明确，交叉账户访问需要明确配置，责任在于用户，而不是AWS的说明不够。

补充讨论：
• abhisek：指出IAM和联合身份的复杂性，认为不是每个弱点都可以被视为漏洞，并质疑是否能找到适合的威胁模型来定义此漏洞。
• gitroom：反思什么是真正的风险，什么是炒作，每个人对风险的定义不同。
• bulatb：批评文章标题和内容简短，暗示这种风格是为了吸引点击。
• ahoka：幽默地指出自己的公司安全套件屏蔽了讨论链接。
• MikeIndyson：强调不应在元数据中存储敏感数据，认为这是实施问题。
• tasuki：认为大多数“安全工具”都会引入安全风险，整个安全行业有其固有的问题和矛盾。

争议焦点：
• 该问题是否构成重大安全风险：一部分人认为这是较小的安全问题，处理得当，而另一部分人则认为这根本不构成安全问题，只是实施中的错误。
• AWS文档是否应更明确地指出最佳实践：有些人认为AWS应更清晰地指导用户，而另一些人则认为这是用户自身的责任。

总结：讨论的核心在于AWS环境中一个被标记为“安全风险”的问题是否真的构成重大威胁，以及责任应归于用户还是AWS的文档说明。不同的技术背景和经验导致了对该问题严重性的不同看法。

43893906.article_content:
Blog
Apr 28, 2025 | 7 min
AWS Built a Security Tool. It Introduced a Security Risk.
Eliav Livneh
Security Researcher
(If you missed the previous parts of this trust policy blog series, we recommend reading parts
one
and
two
first)
In the previous post of this series, we explored four dangerous misconceptions regarding how to securely set up cross-account access in AWS environments.
In this final post of the series, weâll walk through a real-world case where even AWS got it wrong. Their
Account Assessment for AWS Organizations
tool, designed to audit resource-based policies for risky cross-account access, ironically introduced cross-account privilege escalation risks due to flawed deployment instructions. Specifically, customers were effectively encouraged to deploy the tool in lower-sensitivity accounts, creating risky trust paths from insecure environments into highly sensitive ones.
Weâll share how we discovered the issue, the risks it introduced, how AWS fixed it, and what affected organizations should do to detect and remediate it.
How it started
While investigating a critical privilege escalation risk involving an IAM role in a customerâs AWS environment, we discovered a role present in both their production and management accounts, each of which trusted two roles in their development account:
The risky IAM role we investigated
These were the details of the privilege escalation risk (sensitive info redacted):
Examining the permissions of that role in the production and management accounts, we found it had access to several sensitive IAM and data-related API calls, including:
iam:ListRoles
(lists all IAM roles, helping an attacker identify privileged and vulnerable roles)
iam:ListPolicies
(reveals all IAM policies, exposing potential misconfigurations)
secretsmanager:ListSecrets
(lists all stored secret names, identifying potential targets)
s3:ListAllMyBuckets
(enumerates all S3 buckets, exposing potential sensitive data locations)
kms:ListKeys
(lists all encryption keys, indicating what is being encrypted)
kms:GetKeyPolicy
(retrieves key policies, which could reveal weak or misconfigured access controls)
â¦ and more (full policy
here
)
These permissions were granted on all resources (
resource: "*"
), making them particularly dangerous if compromised.
The organization's dev account had weaker security, making this role assumption path a major risk. An attacker compromising a trusted role in dev could immediately gain these permissions in production and management. Combined with other misconfigurations - such as exposed IAM roles, secret names, KMS keys, or public S3 buckets - this could help lead to compromise of the organization's most sensitive accounts.
This was already a serious risk, but what we found next revealed that this misconfiguration was not unique to this organization - it was actually inadvertently encouraged by AWS itself.
Account Assessment for AWS Organizations
The names of these roles were somewhat quirky, and hinted they were part of some automated system. A quick search led us to
Account Assessment for AWS Organizations
, a tool developed by AWS and published in the
AWS Solutions Library
.
According to its official documentation, the tool is designed to âcentrally evaluate and manage AWS accounts within your AWS Organizationsâ, helping users better understand account dependencies. AWS lists its
primary use cases
as mergers and acquisitions, security audits, centralized policy explorer and management account transitions.
So, why was it deployed insecurely?
Given that this tool was built by AWS to audit resource-based cross-account access, we initially assumed the misconfiguration was a deployment error by the customer. However, after reviewing the documentation, we realized that AWSâs deployment instructions unintentionally encouraged insecure setups, making it highly likely that users would deploy the tool in a way that introduced privilege escalation risks.
The tool follows a hub-and-spoke architecture:
A hub role is deployed in a designated hub account.
Spoke roles are deployed in all other accounts to be assessed, trusting the hub role for access.
This design allows the hub role to assume the spoke roles across all accounts, aggregating security data across the organization.
When checking AWS's official deployment guidance, we were surprised to see the following instruction:
"Hub stack - Deploy to any member account in your AWS Organization except the Organizations management account."
This is the root cause of the issue - AWS explicitly recommended not deploying the hub in the management account, without clarifying the security implications of the other possible choices.
Why this is a major security risk
Letâs back up a bit and explain why this instruction, without any clarification, was so problematic.
As we covered in the
previous blog
, allowing a role in a less secure account to assume roles in more sensitive accounts creates a privilege escalation risk.
By d

data.title: Judge said Meta illegally used books to build its AI
data.author: mekpro
data.article_summary: Meta正面临一组包括Sarah Silverman和Ta-Nehisi Coates在内的作家的版权诉讼，核心问题在于Meta的AI工具是否会蚕食作家的书籍销售市场。作家指控Meta非法使用他们的作品来构建其生成式AI工具，尤其是通过“影子图书馆”如LibGen盗版书籍。Meta承认使用了这些作品，但主张其行为受“合理使用”原则保护。美国地方法院法官Vince Chhabria对双方提交的部分简易判决动议进行了审查，焦点在于Meta的AI工具是否会损害作家的商业前景。Chhabria对作者能否提供Meta工具可能损害其销售的证据表示怀疑，并指出如果原告能证明其市场受到影响，Meta可能会败诉。此案的裁决将对生成式AI和版权的法律纠纷产生重要影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Meta使用受版权保护的书籍训练AI模型的合法性及其在法庭上的争议

不同观点：
• 一些评论认为标题具有误导性，因为目前只是关于审前听证会的报道，法官并没有做出裁决。例如，[ndiddy]和[dragonwriter]指出，法官Chhabria对原告能否证明Meta的AI工具会损害作者的商业前景表示怀疑。[granzymes]和[caminanteblanco]也认为标题夸大了实际情况。

• [TimPC]认为原告将案件聚焦于AI生成内容是否影响书籍市场是策略上的错误，因为AI生成的小说质量尚不足以显著影响原作市场。

补充讨论：

43893762.article_content:
Save this story
Save
Save this story
Save
Meta’s
copyright battle
with a group of authors, including Sarah Silverman and Ta-Nehisi Coates, will turn on the question of whether the company’s AI tools produce works that can cannibalize the authors’ book sales.
US District Court Judge Vince Chhabria spent several hours grilling lawyers from both sides after they each filed motions for partial summary judgment, meaning they want Chhabria to rule on specific issues of the case rather than leaving each one to be decided at trial. The authors allege that Meta illegally used their work to build its generative AI tools, emphasizing that the company pirated their books through “shadow libraries” like LibGen. The social media giant is not denying that it used the work or that
it downloaded books from shadow libraries
en masse, but insists that
its behavior is shielded
by the “fair use” doctrine, an exception in US copyright law that allows for permissionless use of copyrighted work in certain cases, including parody, teaching, and news reporting.
If Chhabria grants either motion, he’ll issue a ruling before the case goes to trial—and likely set an important precedent shaping how courts deal with generative AI copyright cases moving forward.
Kadrey v. Meta
is one of the
dozens of lawsuits
filed against AI companies that are winding through the US legal system.
While the authors were heavily focused on the piracy element of the case, Chhabria spoke emphatically about his belief that the big question is whether Meta’s AI tools will hurt book sales and otherwise cause the authors to lose money. “If you are dramatically changing, you might even say obliterating, the market for that person's work, and you're saying that you don't even have to pay a license to that person to use their work to create the product that's destroying the market for their work—I just don't understand how that can be fair use,” he told Meta lawyer Kannon Shanmugam. (Shanmugam responded that the suggested effect was “just speculation.”)
Chhabria and Shanmugam went on to debate whether Taylor Swift would be harmed if her music was fed into an AI tool that then created billions of robotic knockoffs. Chhabria questioned how this would impact less-established songwriters. “What about the next Taylor Swift?” he asked, arguing that a “relatively unknown artist” whose work was ingested by Meta would likely have their career hampered if the model produced “a billion pop songs” in their style.
At times, it sounded like the case was the authors’ to lose, with Chhabria noting that Meta was “destined to fail” if the plaintiffs could prove that Meta’s tools created similar works that cratered how much money they could make from their work. But Chhabria also stressed that he was unconvinced the authors would be able to show the necessary evidence. When he turned to the authors’ legal team, led by high-profile attorney David Boies, Chhabria repeatedly asked whether the plaintiffs could actually substantiate accusations that Meta’s AI tools were likely to hurt their commercial prospects. “It seems like you’re asking me to speculate that the market for Sarah Silverman’s memoir will be affected,” he told Boies. “It’s not obvious to me that is the case.”
When defendants invoke the fair use doctrine, the burden of proof shifts to them to demonstrate that their use of copyrighted works is legal. Boies stressed this point during the hearing, but Chhabria remained skeptical that the authors’ legal team would be able to successfully argue that Meta could plausibly crater their sales. He also appeared lukewarm about whether Meta’s decision to download books from places like LibGen was as central to the fair use issue as the plaintiffs argued it was. “It seems kind of messed up,” he said. “The question, as the courts tell us over and over again, is not whether something is messed up but whether it’s copyright infringement.”
A ruling in the
Kadrey
case could play a pivotal role in the outcomes of the ongoing legal battles over generative AI and copyright. Earlier this spring, a judge
issued a partial summary judgment
in the first AI copyright case,
Thomson Reuters v. Ross
, siding with the publishing conglomerate Thomson Reuters in its fight against AI startup Ross Intelligence. While the ruling was important, that case was an outlier in several ways—including the fact that it didn’t involve generative AI tools like large language models.
The outcome of the Kadrey case is being closely watched—in part because it could shake up Silicon Valley. It will certainly have a major impact on Meta, whether it helps entrench the company’s generative AI strategy or forces a significant shift. CEO Mark Zuckerberg emphasized how central AI is to Meta’s present and future in an earnings call on Wednesday. “Everything that I've talked about today is built on top of our AI models and infrastructure,” he
said
.

data.title: iOS Kindle app now has a ‘get book’ button after changes to App Store rules
data.author: diversion
data.article_summary: Amazon has updated its Kindle iOS app to include a "Get Book" button, allowing users to purchase ebooks directly from the app. This change comes after a recent ruling in the Epic Games v. Apple case, which prevents Apple from collecting a 27% commission on purchases made outside of apps or restricting alternative payment methods. Previously, due to Apple's policies, users had to purchase ebooks through a web browser and then sync them to the app. The new "Get Book" button redirects users to complete purchases via a mobile web browser, streamlining the process. However, if Apple wins its appeal, Amazon may need to revert these changes.

News
Amazon now has a ‘Get book’ button in its iOS Kindle app
Amazon has updated its Kindle iOS app to take advantage of recent changes to Apple’s App Store rules.
Amazon has updated its Kindle iOS app to take advantage of recent changes to Apple’s App Store rules.
by
Andrew Liszewski
May 6, 2025, 1:00 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
The Kindle iOS mobile app now includes a Get Book button for purchasing ebooks.
Screenshot: Amazon
Andrew Liszewski
is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2011, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid.
Following a
ruling on April 30th
by the
Epic Games v. Apple
judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers, Apple can no longer collect a 27 percent commission on purchases made outside of apps or restrict how developers can direct users to alternate payment options. Apple has
appealed the decision
, but is also complying with it in the interim, prompting several companies to
announce app updates
making it
easier for users to pay for subscriptions and services
. That now includes Amazon’s iOS Kindle app. Contrary to prior limitations, there is now a prominent orange “Get book” button on Kindle app’s book listings.
“We regularly make improvements to our apps to help ensure we are providing customers the most convenient experience possible,” Amazon spokesperson Tim Gillman told
The Verge
over email. “By selecting ‘Get Book’ within the Kindle for iOS app, customers can now complete their purchase through their mobile web browser.”
Amazon wasn’t the first company to release a dedicated reading device with an E Ink screen. Companies like Sony beat them to the punch by a couple of years. What helped make the Kindle popular, and arguably destined to dominate the e-reader market, was that you could buy books right on the device, even if you didn’t have Wi-Fi access thanks to
Amazon’s now discontinued cellular Whispernet
service.
Before today’s updates, buying books wasn’t a feature you’d find in the Kindle mobile app following app store rule changes Apple implemented in 2011 that required developers to remove links or buttons leading to alternate ways to make purchases. You could
search for books that offered samples
for download, add them to a shopping list, and read titles you already own, but you couldn’t actually buy titles through the Kindle or Amazon app, or even see their prices.
To avoid having to pay Apple’s 30 percent cut of in-app purchases, and the
27 percent tax on alternative payment methods
Apple introduced in January 2024, Amazon previously required you to visit and login to its online store through a device’s web browser to purchase ebooks on your iPhone or iPad, which were then synchronized to the app. It was a cumbersome process compared to the streamlined experience of buying ebooks directly on a Kindle e-reader.
Amazon probably isn’t going to change its mind about avoiding Apple’s 30 percent cut on ebook sales, but the update to the Kindle app now makes it much easier to purchase ebooks on your iPhone for those times when your Kindle e-reader doesn’t have a reliable Wi-Fi connection.
However, there’s still the chance Apple could win its appeal, forcing Amazon to undo these updates and improvements and once again make buying ebooks on iPhones overcomplicated and inconvenient.

data.title: Brush (Bo(u)rn(e) RUsty SHell) a POSIX and Bash-Compatible Shell in Rust
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary: **Brush** 是一个用 Rust 实现的兼容 POSIX 和 bash 的 shell，支持 Linux 和 macOS，并通过 WSL 在 Windows 上实验性运行。它功能齐全，可作为日常使用的交互式 shell，能执行大多数 sh 和 bash 脚本，但存在一些已知的兼容性限制，如部分 `set` 和 `shopt` 选项未完全实现。目前不建议在生产环境中使用，但欢迎贡献和反馈。安装方式包括通过 `cargo install` 或 Nix、Arch Linux 的 AUR 进行安装。项目采用 MIT 许可，主要通过与现有 shell 对比进行测试，拥有 550+ 个测试案例。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：各类Unix/POSIX兼容的shell以及新 shell 项目的特点和优势

不同观点：
• **支持OSH的看法**：[chubot] 认为 OSH 是少数致力于实现 POSIX/bash 兼容性的 shell，并且具有较高的兼容性和性能优势。它通过“可执行规范”的方式用 Python 编写并翻译为 C++，从而在速度和安全性上优于 bash。OSH 还提供了 YSH，旨在成为终极的粘合语言，支持更结构化的数据处理。

• **对非POSIX shell的兴趣**：[d4mi3n] 更倾向于探索像 Nushell 这样超越传统 POSIX 的 shell，认为文本 stdin/stdout 虽然重要，但更结构化的数据表达和传递方式（如 Nushell 提供的）也很有价值。

• **Fish shell的介绍**：[Pet_Ant] 提到了 Fish shell，它是用 Rust 编写，但既不兼容 POSIX 也不兼容 Bash。Fish 有自己的设计理念，适合那些不追求 POSIX 兼容性的人。

• **跨平台兼容性需求**：[Ericson2314] 关注 shell 在 Windows 上的兼容性，尤其是 Nix on Windows 的情境下，希望找到非 CygWin/MSYS2 的 bash 兼容 shell，以在不同平台上运行现有的 bash 代码。

• **对Rust实现的shell的大小担忧**：[ris] 对用 Rust 编写的 shell（如 Brush）的二进制文件大小表示担忧，认为如果没有共享库支持，难以替代系统基础工具，除非采用类似 busybox 的多调用二进制文件方式。

• **Rust shell的优势疑问**：[hdjrudni] 质疑用 Rust 编写 shell 的卖点，除了速度之外没有看到其他显著优势，并询问是否有相关基准测试。

• **兼容性问题**：[Muromec] 提到 OSH 在与 fzf 脚本配合时存在兼容性问题，具体表现为无法正常使用 fzf 的键绑定和补全脚本。

• **对WSL的使用疑问**：[koakuma-chan] 对在 Windows 上通过 WSL 运行 Brush shell 的实际操作表示疑问，具体询问了运行方式。

• **对新shell的冷漠态度**：[ohroy] 表示虽然新 shell 看起来不错，但没有找到足够的理由从现有工具切换过去。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个用不同语言（Python、C++、Rust）实现的 shell，关注点包括 POSIX 兼容性、性能、数据处理能力、跨平台支持和二进制大小等方面。
• 争议焦点主要在于新 shell 的实际优势和使用场景，特别是在兼容性和性能上的具体表现。
• 部分用户对 Rust 编写的 shell 在二进制文件大小上的表现有所担忧，认为这可能影响其作为系统基础工具的可行性。

brush
About
brush
(
B
o(u)rn(e)
RU
sty
SH
ell) is a
POSIX-
and
bash-
compatible shell,
implemented in Rust. It's built and tested on Linux and macOS, with experimental support on Windows. (Its Linux build is fully supported running on Windows via WSL.)
brush
is functional for interactive use as a daily driver! It can execute most
sh
and
bash
scripts we've
encountered. Known limitations are tracked with filed issues. Out of an abundance of caution,
we wouldn't recommend using it yet in
production
scenarios in case it doesn't behave identically
to your existing stable shell. (If you do find any behavioral differences, though, please report them with an
issue!)
Contributions and feedback of all kinds are welcome! For more guidance, please consult our
contribution guidelines
. For more technical details, please consult the
documentation
in this repo.
This project was originally borne out of curiosity and a desire to learn. We're doing our best to keep that
attitude :).
License
Available for use and distribution under the
MIT license
.
Try it out!
We don't publish binary releases of
brush
, but if you have a working
rust
toolchain installed you can simply run:
cargo install --locked brush-shell
This will install the most recently released version of
brush
from
crates.io
. Alternatively, for the latest and
greatest bits, you can clone this repo and execute
cargo run
.
If you don't have
rust
installed, we recommend installing it via
rustup
.
(If you
are
interested in having a binary release, then please let us know in the 'Discussions' area of this
project or by filing a feature request in 'Issues'.)
If you are a Nix user, you can also use the registered version.
nix run
'
github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixpkgs-unstable#brush
'
-- --version
Arch Linux users can install
brush
from the AUR
with their
AUR helper
of choice, e.g.
paru -S brush
When you run
brush
, it should look exactly as
bash
would on your system since it processes
.bashrc
and
other usual configuration. If you'd like to customize the look of
brush
to distinguish it from the other shells
installed on your system, then you can also author a
~/.brushrc
file.
Known limitations
There are some known gaps in compatibility. Most notably:
Some
set
and
shopt
options.
The
set
builtin is implemented, as is
set -x
and many frequently used
set
/
shopt
options, but a number aren't fully implemented. For example,
set -e
will execute but its semantics aren't applied across execution.
Anything tagged with a
TODO
comment or where
error::unimp()
is used to return a "not implemented" error
.
These aren't all tracked with GitHub issues right now, but there's a number of these scattered throughout the code base. Some are indicative of missing functionality that may be straightforward to implement; others may be more complicated.
If you feel so inclined, we'd love contributions toward any of the above, with broadening test coverage, deeper compatibility evaluation, or really any other opportunities you can find to help us make this project better.
Testing strategy
This project is primarily tested by comparing its behavior with other existing shells, leveraging the latter as test oracles. The integration tests implemented in this repo include
550+ test cases
run on both this shell and an oracle, comparing standard output and exit codes.
For more details, please consult the
reference documentation on integration testing
.
Credits
There's a long list of OSS crates whose shoulders this project rests on. Notably, the following crates are directly relied on for major portions of shell functionality:
reedline
- for readline-like input and interactive usage
clap
- command-line parsing, used both by the top-level brush CLI as well as built-in commands
fancy-regex
- relied on for everything regex
tokio
- async, well, everything
nix
rust crate
- higher-level APIs for Unix/POSIX system APIs

data.title: Preparing for when the machine stops
data.author: foxfired
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了软件开发者在职业生涯中从初学到熟练的过程，以及人工智能（AI）的崛起对开发工作的影响。作者描述了从依赖System 2（慢而分析性的学习模式）到System 1（快而直觉的应用模式）的转变，并通过自身经历说明新技术（如Angular、React、Vue等）如何迫使开发者重新学习。然而，AI的出现不仅改变了开发方式，还质疑了学习本身的必要性。作者警告，过度依赖AI可能导致开发者丧失理解和解决问题的能力，并引用E.M. Forster的小说《机器停转》警示人们，如果完全依赖机器，社会将变得脆弱。文章最后强调，学会如何学习和适时抵制自动化带来的便利同样重要，因为当“机器停止”时，我们需要重新学会思考。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对技术进步、自动化及未来社会系统的思考与担忧

不同观点：
• **对技术依赖的担忧**：
  - strict9、lurk2、metalrain等人认为，随着技术（尤其是AI和自动化）的发展，年轻一代逐渐失去对基础技能和知识的掌握。当系统崩溃时，社会将无法维持，因为没有人知道如何修复这些系统（如The Machine Stops中的情境）。
  - strict9特别指出，技术行业的工作机会减少以及过度依赖AI会导致未来技术系统维护的困难。
  - metalrain强调，如果发生大规模的电子设备损坏（如EMP事件），依赖软件工作的人将失去能力修复或重建技术系统。

• **对技术进步的乐观态度**：
  - hnthrow90348765认为，即便发生大规模技术崩溃，人类可以在相对较短的时间内通过书籍和其他知识来源重建技术能力。并指出，即使经历10年的“黑暗时代”，人类仍然在技术上保持领先。
  - cadamsdotcom反驳了单一崩溃点的担忧，认为人类已经建立了没有单一崩溃点的系统，且AI模型已经多样化，来自不同的文化和国家。

• **对自动化与人类技能的平衡讨论**：

43909111.article_content:
For over two decades, I’ve worked as a software developer. At some point along the way, writing JavaScript stopped being something I had to think about, it just happened. Building CRUD apps, managing forms, handling the DOM, these became second nature. I could step into almost any project and instantly start wiring things up. This is what Daniel Kahneman refers to as
System 1 thinking
: fast, intuitive, automatic.
But that ease didn’t come for free. It was built through years of deliberate effort, of debugging endless edge cases, of reading through documentation line by line. That’s
System 2
: slow, analytical, and effortful. It’s what you use when you’re learning something new, when you don’t yet have mental shortcuts to fall back on.
As developers, we constantly shift between these two modes. The longer we work in the field, the more we rely on System 1. Until the ground shifts beneath our feet.
I remember the first time I used Angular 1.0. Coming from the jQuery world, it felt completely foreign. Suddenly, my deep, intuitive knowledge meant little. I had to slow down, re-learn, and question my assumptions. But over time, as I built more Angular apps, it too became second nature. System 2 became System 1.
And then Angular 2.0 dropped. The whole model changed. It wasn’t just an update, it was a paradigm shift. Everything I had internalized had to be re-evaluated.
Now it’s React, Vue, or Svelte. Each framework comes with its own philosophy, patterns, and quirks. When I start working with one, I’m back to Googling everything I type. I’m in System 2 again. But I know the pattern. I’ve been here before. Slowly, it becomes intuitive.
But just as I settle into this new rhythm, AI enters the scene. Not as a new tool, but as a paradigm shift. One that doesn’t just require learning. It questions whether we need to learn at all.
Today, AI can scaffold entire applications, write components, even solve obscure bugs. With tools like GitHub Copilot and ChatGPT, it’s easy to get by without deeply understanding the code you’re deploying. At first, this feels empowering. But there’s a hidden cost.
To understand that cost, think about riding a horse. For centuries, humans relied on horses for transportation. It was a skill everyone needed. Then the automobile came along and replaced the horse. We didn’t lose much, because driving still required
some
form of System 2 engagement. We had to learn, we had to adapt.
But what happens when the car drives itself?
In E.M. Forster’s short story
The Machine Stops
, he paints a future where a vast machine handles every aspect of human life. People live isolated lives, fully dependent on the machine. They don’t know how it works. They only know how to ask it for things. When the machine breaks down, society collapses. No one remembers how to fix it.
This is the danger of bypassing both System 1 and System 2. If we no longer struggle to learn (System 2), and no longer build intuition (System 1), we become entirely dependent on tools we don’t understand. We trade capability for convenience.
In my personal work, I avoid chasing trends. I choose tools that are battle-tested. Tools I can reason about. Sure, at work, I use whatever the job demands. But when I build for myself, I want to understand every line.
Learning to learn is a noble idea. But more important is learning to unlearn, and knowing when to resist the comfort of automation. Because one day, when the machine stops, we’ll need to remember how to think.

data.title: TeleMessage, used by Trump officials, can access plaintext chat logs
data.author: micahflee
data.article_summary: 文章揭示了TeleMessage公司开发的修改版Signal应用（TM SGNL）存在的严重安全漏洞。该应用被特朗普政府高官使用，但TeleMessage可以访问用户的明文聊天记录。文章详细分析了TM SGNL的Android源代码，指出该应用将聊天记录存档到TeleMessage服务器，使其能够获取明文信息。尽管与官方Signal应用外观和功能相似，但TM SGNL用户在注册时通过官方Signal服务器，而聊天数据却被TeleMessage保存。文章还提到，黑客攻击证实了这些安全问题，TeleMessage服务器存储了Signal、WhatsApp、Telegram等聊天记录的明文副本。参议员Ron Wyden已要求司法部调查此事，认为其对美国国家安全构成威胁。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对特朗普官员使用Signal克隆版本的技术分析及其安全性讨论

不同观点：
• [质疑不负责任的网络安全实践] dogman144认为，当这一事件首次曝光时，部分Hacker News（HN）用户声称这是高明的网络安全策略（4D chess），而不是不负责任的网络安全实践。他认为这种观点无论当时还是现在都是错误的，因为这个事件暴露了供应链风险，且如果是故意设计的策略，那也是极其糟糕的执行结果。最终，这种不安全的设置在国家安全领域被利用了。

• [对分析深度的质疑] mmooss指出，在这个HN讨论串中，目前还没有特别实质性的分析，大家对此也无从深入评论。他认为HN的许多评论者不会在快速写下的评论中犯这种错误。

• [批评政府行为] fnordpiglet批评政府试图监禁像Krebs这样诚实的人，认为他们得到了应得的“专家”。

• [实用性问题] proactivesvcs提到，Signal没有提供在任何平台上以明文形式访问聊天记录的功能，这使得备份变得困难。尤其是在桌面端，由于数据库的变化，备份程序需要不断更新，这带来了不便。

• [对安全漏洞的讽刺] aeontech讽刺地表示，与其黑进手机安装键盘记录器，不如说服公司的IT部门直接购买和安装。

• [对潜在风险的担忧] csours和theyknowitsxmas认为，这个事件可能带来潜在的安全风险（footgun），但任何人都可以修改客户端名称并在公开场合误导他人。

• [为特朗普政府辩护] khaky54为特朗普政府使用Signal克隆版本的行为进行辩护，指出这种做法实际上是为了遵守法律和机构政策，并且相关的基础设施是在上届政府期间设置的。他还引用了多个来源和配置说明，证明该系统在理论上是安全的，尤其是对于敏感的政府通信。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于特朗普政府使用Signal克隆版本的意图和安全性。一部分人认为这是不负责任的网络安全实践，而另一部分人则认为这是为了遵守法律和政策的需要，且系统设置在理论上是安全的。

• 讨论中还涉及了具体技术细节，例如消息的加密传输路径，是否经过商业云服务，以及政府部门使用的不同安全等级配置。这些技术细节进一步复杂化了对整个事件的安全性评估。

• 讨论还提到，最初的报道可能带有误导性，将特朗普政府的行为描述为异常或违法，而实际上这种做法可能是前几届政府就开始的标准操作。

Despite their misleading marketing, TeleMessage, the company that makes a modified version of Signal used by senior Trump officials, can access plaintext chat logs from its customers.
In this post I give a high level overview of how the TeleMessage fake Signal app, called TM SGNL, works and why it's so insecure. Then I give a thorough analysis of the source code for TM SGNL's Android app, and what led me to conclude that TeleMessage can access plaintext chat logs. Finally, I back up my analysis with as-of-yet unpublished details about the
hack
of TeleMessage.
But first, here's a quick timeline of events.
On Thursday, 404 Media
reported
that in the Reuters
photo
showing former National Security Advisor and
war criminal
Mike Waltz checking his Signal messages under the table, he was actually using an obscure modified Signal app called TM SGNL, and not the real and actually secure Signal app.
On Friday, I wrote
an analysis
of everything I could find out about TM SGNL using OSINT, including the fact that it's nearly impossible to install without a device enrolled in an MDM service that's tied to an Apple Business Manager or a Google Enterprise account.
On Saturday, after
discovering
that TeleMessage
published
the source code for the TM SGNL apps for Android and iPhone themselves, I
re-published them
on GitHub with the goal of making them easier to research. (It looks like the iOS source code is actually just unmodified Signal, so maybe they actually only published their Android code.)
On Saturday night, an anonymous source told me they hacked TeleMessage.
On Sunday, I, along with Joseph Cox,
published an article
about the hack to 404 Media (and to
my blog
).
On Monday, NBC News
reported
that TeleMessage suspended its service after a
second hacker
breached TeleMessage and "downloaded a large cache of files."
Today, Senator Ron Wyden
published
a letter, which cites the 404 Media article and my analysis of TM SGNL, to Attorney General Pam Bondi, requesting that the Justice Department investigate the "serious threat to U.S. national security posed by TeleMessage, a federal contractor that sold dangerously insecure communications software to the White House and other federal agencies."
The devastating hacks confirm the analysis that I'm sharing in this post: that TeleMessage's server –  hosted on the public AWS cloud, run by an
Israeli company
that's lead by a former IDF spook – has plaintext access to the Signal chat logs they're archiving (along with chat logs for Telegram, WeChat, and WhatsApp).
If you find this interesting,
subscribe
to get these posts emailed directly to your inbox. If you want to support my work, considering becoming a paid supporter.

Overview
TeleMessage makes modified versions of popular messaging apps, including Signal, WhatsApp, Telegram, and WeChat. The modified Signal app is almost entirely identical to the authentic version of Signal, except it also archives copies of every message to a destination determined by the TeleMessage customer. (Presumably, WhatsApp, Telegram, and WeChat work in the same way, but I have only analyzed the TM SGNL for Android source code.)
The TM SGNL app
TM SGNL is interoperable with Signal. When a TM SGNL user registers a new account, they're registering it with the official Signal server. TM SGNL users can send messages to Signal users and visa versa. If you're a Signal user, you have no way of knowing when you're talking to a TM SGNL user, because the apps are nearly identical and use the same infrastructure.
This is how Mike Waltz could accidentally add The Atlantic editor-in-chief Jeffrey Goldberg to a group chat where they discussed
bombing an apartment building full of civilians
: Waltz was presumably using TM SGNL, and Goldberg was presumably using Signal.
Note that we don't know how long Trump officials have been using TM SGNL. It's possible they've been using it since around Trump's inauguration on January 20. If this is the case, the chat logs for the Signal group where Waltz invited Goldberg will have been collected by TeleMessage. But it's also possible that they only started using TM SGNL
after
Signalgate, maybe as a way to attempt to start complying with record keeping laws. So far, we don't know the timeline. This would be good to get to the bottom of to understand what laws they have already broken.

• 讨论还提到，最初的报道可能带有误导性，将特朗普政府的行为描述为异常或违法，而实际上这种做法可能是前几届政府就开始的标准操作。

data.title: Will supercapacitors come to AI's rescue?
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了人工智能（AI）工作负载对电力需求的快速波动可能对电网造成压力，尤其是在需要短时高功率的情况下。为解决这一问题，数据中心正引入超级电容器组。超级电容器能够快速充放电，适合应对AI计算中突发的电力需求高峰，从而减轻对电网的负担。这一方案由西门子能源等公司推动，旨在提升数据中心电力系统的稳定性和效率。文章强调，超级电容器可能成为应对AI电力挑战的关键解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何应对AI工作负载带来的电力需求波动

不同观点：
• [tzs] 提出一种通过在无峰值时进行虚拟计算来平衡电力需求的方案，但指出这会导致能源浪费，并讽刺有人可能结合LLM和加密货币挖矿以利用峰值间的空闲资源。
• [0cf8612b2e1e] 建议使用备用电源和电池来应对电力需求波动，但质疑这种方法对电池快速降解的影响，并提到现有太阳能设施已有类似操作。
• [blt] 质疑AI工作负载产生需求 burst 的原因，认为AI训练应是持续性的，而非爆发性的。
• [WatchDog] 认为通过调整软件来解决电力需求波动问题会更经济。
• [Merrill] 建议优化网络和软件以持续利用GPU资源，避免设备在计算间隙闲置，并提到DeepSeek曾采用类似方法提高性能。
• [sonium] 以幽默方式提到使用 "pytorch.powerplant_no_blow_up operator" 来解决问题，暗示通过软件手段处理电力需求。
• [Animats] 质疑大数据中心的负载波动对电网的实际影响，认为其他如电炉或轧机等负载对电网影响更大。
• [bcoates] 关注数据中心的冷却问题，建议通过调节压缩机电机来控制温度，而非依赖被动冷却。
• [janalsncm] 对GPU集群的负载曲线感兴趣，建议在网络间隙期间引入次级工作负载，并提到GPU运行时的物理噪音（如线圈噪音）可反映其工作状态。
• [paulkrush] 提出使用超级电容器来简化软件设计、降低延迟和成本的可能性。
• [amelius] 认为超导超级电感可能是更好的解决方案。
• [lawlessone] 简单否定了上述某些建议。
• [hulitu] 以讽刺语气回应超级电容器拯救AI电力需求波动的可能性，暗示对此持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于如何有效平衡AI训练中的电力需求波动，具体方法包括硬件（如备用电池、超级电容器、超导材料）和软件优化（调整软件逻辑或引入次级工作负载）。
- 电池降解、GPU闲置成本、冷却问题和电网实际承受能力等都是讨论中涉及的重要论据。
- 部分评论带有幽默和讽刺，反映了对某些技术方案可行性的怀疑态度。
